text: The Krieger–Nelson Prize is awarded by the Canadian Mathematical Society to recognize an outstanding woman in mathematics. It was first given in 1995 and is named after Cecilia Krieger and Evelyn Nelson, both of whom made significant contributions to mathematics in Canada. While the prize is primarily awarded to a female mathematician employed at a Canadian university, it has also been given to Canadian-born or -educated women working abroad. For instance, Cathleen Morawetz, who served as past president of the American Mathematical Society and was a faculty member at the Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences (a division of New York University), received the prize in 1997. Morawetz was educated at the University of Toronto in Canada. The award guidelines specify that the recipient should be a "member of the Canadian mathematical community." The recipient is required to deliver a lecture to the Canadian Mathematical Society, usually during its summer meeting.
